text:
incident-bot: PAGER: runtime-prod GPU pool reporting surge in OOMs and elevated p50 token latency. 48 ENOMEMs in 5m window. Paging oncall-jin.

oncall-jin: on it. acked. quick status: which model/pool/tenants affected?

mara: errors are hitting /v1/generate for model=redwood-large-quant in prod-us-east. Top affected customers: tenant-A, tenant-B, a few less-active tenants. Runtime returning 502/ENOMEM.

sam: metrics show correlation with a deploy at 2026-03-15T16:20Z. That rollout changed default batch_size from 8 -> 12 for this model. OOMs start ~16:22Z.

lee: pasting a few relevant logs from worker-12 here.

mara: ```
[16:23:11] runtime alloc: cudaMalloc(1.2GiB) -> ERROR ENOMEM
[16:23:11] worker=worker-12 model=redwood-large-quant batch_size=12 kv_cache_slots=512
[16:23:12] fallback: routed to cpu-variant redwood-large-quant-cpu
```

oncall-jin: preliminary hypotheses: (A) higher batch_size increased peak per-batch allocations causing fragmentation OOMs; (B) KV cache allocation layout and slot count causing fragmented arenas; (C) recent allocator/kernel changes in runtime causing non-coalescing frees. Need quick mitigations: reduce batch_size via route override, lower kv_cache_slots, or rollback the deploy.

ashley: starting rolling restarts in runtime-prod GPU pool to clear fragmentation: 2 workers at a time. ETA ~6m for first window. Do you want me to also push config overrides?

oncall-jin: yes. push a route override for model=redwood-large-quant in runtime-prod: batch_size=4, kv_cache_slots=256. Keep scope narrow to avoid affecting other models.

sam: executing: 
```
redwoodctl routes update --pool runtime-prod --model redwood-large-quant --set batch_size=4 --set kv_cache_slots=256 --strategy route-only
```

sam: applied route override. monitoring for OOM counts and error rates.

mara: customer impact: tenant-A saw ~15% failed requests in last 10m, tenant-B ~8%. CS should be notified. @ops-bot please open a customer-impact ticket and page CS oncall.

ops-bot: created ticket INC-2026-301 and paged CS-oncall.

lee: after override + two-worker restart: OOM count dropped to 4 in the last 5m. p50 token latency also dropped back closer to baseline. Still seeing intermittent ENOMEMs at peaks.

oncall-jin: good progress. Next: collect GPU memory snapshots and allocator state from affected workers (worker-12, worker-9, worker-15). @mara can you pull nvidia-smi -q and runtime allocator dump from worker-12 before it recycles? Put them in the incident share.

mara: uploaded: /incidents/1784501234/gpu-smi-worker12.log and /incidents/1784501234/alloc-map-worker12.txt

mara: excerpt:
```
# nvidia-smi capture
GPU 0 total mem: 24576 MiB, used ~22000 MiB by python processes
# allocator dump excerpt
free_chunks: many small free holes interleaved, largest_free=320MiB, largest_alloc_request=1.2GiB -> allocation failed
kv_cache: 512 slots allocated, avg slot ~1.5MiB, fragmented layout observed
```

oncall-jin: notes: fragmentation pattern matches theory: total free memory > requested allocation but no contiguous chunk large enough -> classic fragmentation. Could be exacerbated by large batch allocation patterns or kv_cache slab layout.

sam: did a quick canary: disabled KV cache on worker-3 (KV_CACHE_ENABLED=false). That worker handled requests without ENOMEM for 10m under similar load.

lee: options for mitigation/tests: (1) keep route override to smaller batch_size and lower kv_cache_slots; (2) try compacting allocator or larger slab sizes — higher risk mid-incident; (3) rollback deploy that increased batch_size. For RCA, we should reproduce locally with same sequence of allocations.

ashley: I can spin up a canary pool in us-east with batch_size=2 kv_cache_slots=128 and route small % (5%) of traffic. Will report results in ~10m.

oncall-jin: do it. Also maintain timeline entries and hypothesis owners here.

Timeline (owner):
- 16:20 deploy: changed default batch_size 8->12 (owner: infra-release)
- 16:22 OOM spike detected by incident-bot (oncall-jin acknowledged)
- 16:24 initial triage and hypotheses (oncall-jin)
- 16:30 route override applied: batch_size=4 kv_cache_slots=256 (sam)
- 16:34 rolling restarts start (ashley)
- 16:40 OOMs drop but intermittent ENOMEMs persist (lee)

Hypotheses (tracking):
H1: Increased batch_size causes per-request allocation patterns that require a large contiguous chunk, leading to fragmentation OOM. severity: high. evidence: timing with deploy + drop after override. owner: sam
H2: KV cache slot allocation and slab layout increases fragmentation pressure. severity: medium. evidence: canary with KV disabled worked. owner: mara
H3: Allocator/kernel selection bug introduced in recent runtime change resulting in non-coalescing frees. severity: medium. evidence: allocator dumps show many small free chunks not coalescing. owner: lee

mara: next steps for RCA: collect full allocator traces from three affected workers, reproduce workload locally with same batch patterns, add a synthetic test to the CI that simulates frequent large alloc/free with KV slots interleaved.

oncall-jin: comms: post mitigation note to status page that we reduced batch_size and kv cache settings and are investigating root cause. Ashley to draft message.

ashley: status posted: "Mitigation applied: reduced batch size and KV cache config for affected model in prod-us-east. Some customers experienced transient failures; engineering is investigating." :thumbsup:

oncall-jin: keep this thread as the single source for RCA coordination. If OOMs reappear at scale, escalate to rollback of the deploy. Monitoring window for this incident: 30m from mitigation. Thanks everyone for quick responses.

(attachments saved in incident folder: gpu-smi-worker12.log, alloc-map-worker12.txt, route-change-audit.log)
